fields.subject: index_patient
fields.name: Ginkgo biloba extract
fields.regimen: 80 mg twice a day for 2 months (24 mg of glicosides Ginkgo-flavonoids and 6 mg of terpene lactones)

facts.clinical_statement: Medication withdrawn
facts.notes: "the medication" refers to the Ginkgo biloba extract; withdrawal date not stated.

fields.subject: index_patient
fields.action_text: Counseling in easy language on definition of hyperacusis and tinnitus, their possible etiologies and association, and decreasing constant ear protection use

evidence.quote: Treatment was composed by: - Counseling using an easy language, including the definition of hyperacusis and tinnitus, their possible etiologies and association, as well as the need to decrease the constant use of ear protection, which is likely to worsen the sound intolerance.

facts.clinical_statement: Counseling given as part of the treatment
facts.notes: "Treatment was composed by" states the counseling as delivered treatment content.

fields.subject: index_patient
fields.action_text: Environmental low level sound therapy for 2–3 h during the day or night

evidence.quote: Use of environmental low level sound therapy for 2–3 h during the day or night. However, PFB disagreed because he was afraid of withdrawing ear protection.
The concomitant use of environmental sound, as mentioned above, was reinforced.
He did not adhere to using environmental sound.

facts.clinical_statement: Environmental low level sound therapy proposed; patient disagreed and did not adhere
facts.notes: Disagreement and non-adherence are also kept as outcomes items.

summary.text: A 12-year-old male came for a first visit in February 2013 with sound intolerance to the voices of family, friends and teachers, radio, TV and traffic. He limited school activities, wore ear protection all day, spent recess in the library, and had constant high-frequency bilateral tinnitus that began two months earlier. Ear, nose and throat examination was normal.

Serial audiological batteries between March 2013 and February 2014 recorded hearing thresholds, loudness discomfort levels, tinnitus pitch and loudness, and minimal masking levels in both ears. Treatment comprised counseling, environmental low level sound therapy that he disagreed with and did not adhere to, and Ginkgo biloba extract 80 mg twice a day for 2 months, prescribed because of his resistance and the presence of short-term tinnitus; in May 2013 it was suggested to keep the medication for a further three months.

In May 2013 he noticed gradual improvement of tinnitus and hyperacusis, and in August 2013 he reported greater improvement, decreased ear protection use and stopped spending recess in the library. Because of the extra improvement the medication was withdrawn, and after six months in February 2014 the improvement was kept stable with no further treatment.

summary.text: An 11-year-old male came for a first visit in November 2013, his parents having searched for help outside their country, with long-standing sound intolerance to many sounds, especially for the last 8 months, using ear protection continuously at school, street and home. He had no past or present history of tinnitus, and the ear, nose and throat examination was normal.

The audiological examination, citing the Nov 2012 audiometry and loudness discomfort levels brought by the patient, showed normal bilateral hearing thresholds, levels from 80 to 90 dB in both ears and normal acoustic reflexes. After his parents were oriented about the empiric evidence, he was advised Ginkgo biloba extract plus environmental sounds for 3 months, the same schedule was tried, and he performed tinnitus retraining therapy regularly.

In May 2014 parents noticed improved behavior when facing sounds and rare ear protection use, and he was advised to keep environmental sounds at night and decrease the extract to one pill a day for another month. In August 2014 he enjoyed birthday parties with friends and music, and both treatments were withdrawn.
